images.title: Pair each 10 with a 5
images.purpose: Shows 10⁴ ÷ 5⁴ as four 10s over four 5s, each column giving 2, so the result is 2⁴, which is 16.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. One large fraction in the centre with four columns, and the result on the right.
images.exact_structure: A long horizontal fraction bar. Above it, exactly 4 teal (#0072B2) boxes each showing '10'; below it, exactly 4 amber (#E69F00) boxes each showing '5', one directly under each 10. Each of the 4 columns is enclosed by a thin reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded outline, and under each column is a small reddish purple (#CC79A7) circle showing '2'. To the left of the fraction, the label '10⁴ ÷ 5⁴'. To the right, an arrow to the label '2⁴' and then '16' in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box. Exactly 8 boxes, 4 outlines, 4 circles, 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: With equal exponents, divide the bases and keep the exponent: 10⁴ ÷ 5⁴ = 2⁴ = 16.
images.description: Shows 10⁴ ÷ 5⁴ as four 10s over four 5s, each column giving 2, so the result is 2⁴, which is 16.

image_decisions.why: Pairing each 10 with a 5 is the reason the bases divide while the exponent stays, which is this concept.
